method: Align one function's instruction streams in two titles (resyncing on shape, requiring the same bytes outside the numeric fields) and report every memory displacement that moved. A relocation of one function keeps its bytes and changes its operands, so an aligned pair whose only differences are numeric is the evidence that a field moved. The pairing quality and the alignment ratio are printed with every answer; the tool's self-check is the identical-title round trip.
checks: self-check: source == target, address == address -> 0 moved displacements of 60 aligned pairs, alignment 1.000, operand-shape agreement 1.000
systematic frame shift as the alignment's own witness: the executor's frame is 8 bytes smaller in th12 (sub esp,0x310 -> 0x308) and six stack displacements each move by exactly -8

round 305 measured the laser manager pair and added 21 field rows carrying record=laser-manager; the rows from the enemy executor carry record=enemy-record, because a bare offset can name a field in two different records and the disagreement over nothing else is where that was seen
note: Measured so far on the enemy/ECL command executor (th11 0x412e30 <-> th12 0x004154d0). Both record fields the executor touches moved by the SAME +0x138, which is why one row can describe them together; whether every field of that record follows it needs further functions measured, and that is the next round's item.

rows.role: enemy record: pointer to the enemy object the command acts on (the executor's first substantive instruction, `mov esi,[ebx+0x1614]` / `mov esi,[ebx+0x174c]`)
evidence: aligned pair 0x412e72 -> 0x415512, `mov esi, dword ptr [ebx + 0x1614]` against `mov esi, dword ptr [ebx + 0x174c]`, all other bytes identical
acceptance by use: with the map absent the executor read 0 and died at pc=0x415518 (`mov eax,[esi+4]`, address 0x4)

rows.role: enemy record: the 32-bit state flags the executor tests (`test dword [ebx+0x1580],0x400000` against `test dword [ebx+0x16b8],0x2000000`)
evidence: aligned pair 0x412ef1 -> 0x41558d; the flag immediate also moved (0x400000 -> 0x2000000), a constant of the same structure, and constants are reported separately by the tool (--constants)
